meta.phase: Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC)

cross_references.notes: The Africa CDC PHECS briefing (2026-05-18) provides the most-cited headline aggregates of 395 suspected cases and 106 deaths across DRC+Uganda; the CDC current-situation page (2026-05-18) gives 11 confirmed, 336 suspected, 88 deaths in DRC + 2 confirmed/1 death Uganda; OCHA (2026-05-19) gives the highest figure yet of 482 suspected cases and 116 deaths in Ituri alone — discrepancy reflects rapid case ascertainment and different geographic scopes; figures are aligned directionally across all primary sources.

locations.name: Rwampara Health Zone
locations.notes: Likely ground-zero health zone; 8 of 13 initial blood samples tested positive here confirming Bundibugyo virus on 15 May 2026; six health areas within the zone affected.

locations.name: Mongbwalu Health Zone
locations.notes: High-traffic artisanal gold-mining area believed to be the original spillover site; WHO was first alerted on 5 May 2026 to a high-mortality cluster here including four health-worker deaths within four days.

locations.name: Bunia Health Zone (provincial capital)
locations.notes: Provincial capital and urban hub; index case — a healthcare worker with onset 24 April 2026 — died at a medical centre here; at least one confirmed American (Dr. Peter Stafford) tested positive in Bunia on 17 May 2026.

locations.name: Goma
locations.notes: Laboratory-confirmed case announced 17–18 May 2026 by INRB director Muyembe; patient is the wife of a Bunia man who died of Ebola and travelled to Goma while already infected; M23 rebels confirmed isolation; Rwanda closed border crossings in response.

locations.name: Beni
locations.notes: Confirmed case reported evening 17 May 2026; patient travelled from Bunia according to North Kivu provincial minister of social affairs; confirms spread of Bundibugyo virus within North Kivu.

locations.name: Kampala
locations.notes: Two unrelated laboratory-confirmed imported cases; first: 59-year-old Congolese male admitted Kibuli Muslim Hospital 11 May, died 14 May; second: a separate individual with no epidemiological link to Case 1, confirmed 16 May 2026; no local transmission identified as of 18 May.

locations.name: Kinshasa
locations.notes: An individual returning from Ituri to Kinshasa initially flagged as a case on 16 May 2026 but tested negative on confirmatory INRB PCR testing; WHO formally retracted this case.

timeline.event: Index case — a nurse — presents with fever, hemorrhage, vomiting and malaise at a medical centre in Bunia, Ituri Province, DRC; later dies. (WHO DON602 / DRC MoH)

Suspected index case — a nurse at Evangelical Medical Centre, Bunia — develops fever, bleeding, and severe weakness; dies within days. Retrospective investigation suggests she was infected by a patient, implying community transmission was already ongoing.
Earliest known suspected case — a healthcare worker in Bunia — reports symptom onset (fever, hemorrhaging, vomiting); dies at Bunia medical centre. (WHO DON602)
Index case: healthcare worker in Bunia develops fever, haemorrhaging, vomiting and intense malaise — first known suspected case of the outbreak, later dies at a Bunia medical centre.
Cluster of unexplained haemorrhagic fever deaths flagged in Mongbwalu, Ituri Province, DRC.
WHO alerted to a high-mortality outbreak of unknown etiology in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri, including deaths of four health workers within four days. (WHO DON602)
WHO alerted to high-mortality unknown illness in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri Province, including deaths among healthcare workers; initial GeneXpert tests in Bunia return negative for Zaire Ebola.
WHO alerted to high-mortality unknown illness cluster in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri Province, including 4 healthcare worker deaths within 4 days. (WHO DON602)
WHO alerted to high-mortality cluster of unknown illness in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri Province, including 4 health-worker deaths within 4 days.
MSF receives alerts of increased hemorrhagic fever deaths in Mongbwalu; team deployed finds 55 deaths since early April. (MSF statement)
Rapid-response teams investigate Mongbwalu and Rwampara HZs; 13 blood samples collected and sent to INRB Kinshasa for advanced analysis. (WHO DON602)
WHO rapid-response team conducts in-depth investigation in Mongbwalu and Rwampara health zones. (WHO DON602)
WHO/DRC rapid-response teams conduct in-depth field investigation in Mongbwalu and Rwampara Health Zones; samples collected and sent to INRB Kinshasa.
INRB Kinshasa analyses samples; PCR confirms Orthoebolavirus in 8 of 13 specimens; genomic sequencing identifies Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). (WHO DON602 / INRB)
INRB Kinshasa analyses 13 blood samples from Rwampara Health Zone; 8 confirmed Orthoebolavirus-positive by PCR on 15 May. Second Uganda imported case confirmed in Kampala on 16 May.
INRB Kinshasa analyses 13 blood samples from Rwampara; 8 test positive by PCR for Orthoebolavirus. (WHO DON602)
INRB analyses 13 blood samples from Rwampara Health Zone; 8 test positive for Orthoebolavirus by PCR; results released 15 May.
Bundibugyo virus confirmed by laboratory (8 of 13 samples positive). First confirmed case detected in Kampala, Uganda.

DRC Ministry of Public Health officially declares the 17th Ebola outbreak; Uganda MoH confirms imported BVD case — 59-year-old Congolese male who died at Kibuli Muslim Hospital, Kampala, on 2026-05-14. (DRC MoH / Uganda MoH / Africa CDC)
Africa CDC activates Incident Management Support Team; convenes urgent cross-border coordination meeting with DRC, Uganda, South Sudan, WHO and partners. (Africa CDC)

DRC MoH officially declares 17th Ebola outbreak; INRB confirms 8 positive samples by PCR, genomic sequencing identifies Bundibugyo virus. Uganda MoH confirms first imported case — a 59-year-old Congolese man who died at Kibuli Muslim Hospital, Kampala.

INRB genomic sequencing confirms Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). DRC MoH officially declares the 17th Ebola outbreak. Uganda MoH confirms first imported case (died 14 May in Kampala). Africa CDC issues urgent regional coordination call. (WHO DON602; Africa CDC)

DRC MoH officially declares 17th Ebola outbreak in DRC; genomic sequencing confirms Bundibugyo virus (BDBV/Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense). Uganda MoH simultaneously declares outbreak following first confirmed imported case in Kampala (Kibuli Muslim Hospital). Africa CDC convenes urgent high-level regional coordination meeting with DRC, Uganda, South Sudan and 130+ global partners.
Second confirmed Kampala case (fatal). Suspected Kinshasa case reported (later retracted).
Second imported confirmed case identified in Kampala with no apparent link to the first; suspected Kinshasa case tests negative on confirmatory INRB PCR and is disconfirmed. (WHO PHEIC / INRB)
WHO Director-General determines the Bundibugyo outbreak in DRC and Uganda constitutes a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC); does not meet pandemic emergency criteria. (WHO)

WHO Director-General declares PHEIC for Bundibugyo Ebola in DRC and Uganda; determination cites 8 confirmed, 246 suspected, 80 deaths in Ituri plus 2 confirmed cases in Kampala and 4 HCW deaths. Africa CDC holds 130-participant high-level consultative meeting.

Second imported case confirmed in Kampala (unlinked to first). WHO Director-General determines outbreak constitutes a PHEIC. 246 suspected cases, 80 suspected deaths in Ituri confirmed at this time-point. (WHO PHEIC declaration)

Second unrelated confirmed case reported in Kampala, Uganda. WHO Director-General declares a PHEIC under IHR Article 12 — without convening an Emergency Committee, citing the gravity of the situation. Africa CDC activates its Incident Management Support Team.
WHO Director-General declares Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC).

INRB/AFP confirms Goma case: wife of a Bunia Ebola fatality tested positive after traveling to Goma (North Kivu) while already infected, extending geographic spread beyond Ituri. (INRB via AFP / Al Jazeera)

An American healthcare worker in DRC tests positive for Bundibugyo virus disease; CDC and US State Dept coordinate medical evacuation to Germany for treatment; 6 additional high-risk contacts also moved to Germany. (CDC / NBC News)

An American healthcare worker in DRC tests positive for Ebola Bundibugyo; US officials coordinate evacuation of seven individuals to Germany for care. CDC confirms Level 2 travel health notice for DRC, Level 1 for Uganda.
WHO Emergency Committee to be convened; WHO Director-General confirms PHEIC declared without prior Emergency Committee recommendation — a first in WHO history, citing extraordinary urgency.
WHO formally announces PHEIC; does not declare pandemic emergency. INRB confirms first case in Goma (North Kivu) — wife of Bunia fatality. (WHO; INRB via AFP)
US missionary physician Dr. Peter Stafford tests positive for Bundibugyo virus at Nyankunde Hospital near Bunia; CDC confirms an American has tested positive. (Serge charity; CDC briefing)

INRB Director Muyembe confirms laboratory-positive case in Goma, North Kivu (M23-held city of >1 million, on Rwandan border). Confirmed case also reported in Beni, North Kivu. Rwanda closes Goma–Gisenyi border crossings indefinitely. American missionary physician Dr. Peter Stafford tests positive for Bundibugyo virus in Bunia; CDC confirms first US national infected.
Outbreak expands from 3 to 9+ health zones in DRC. New confirmed case in Goma (under M23 rebel control). US CDC enacts enhanced travel screening.
Africa CDC declares outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS); reports ~395 suspected cases and 106 associated deaths across DRC and Uganda. (Africa CDC)

CDC and DHS implement enhanced US travel screening, Title 42 entry restrictions on non-US passport holders who traveled to DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan in the prior 21 days; CDC EOC activated. (CDC / DHS)

CDC Situation Summary (most recent official update) reports 11 confirmed cases and 336 suspected cases including 88 deaths in DRC, and 2 confirmed cases including 1 death in Uganda across 9 health zones. (CDC Situation Summary)

Africa CDC declares outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS); 395 suspected cases and 106 deaths confirmed. US CDC/DHS invoke Title 42, restricting entry of non-US passport holders who have been in DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan in prior 21 days.

Ebola confirmed in Goma, North Kivu (rebel-held M23 city); Rwanda closes Goma-Gisenyi border crossings. Confirmed case also reported in Beni, North Kivu. DRC Health Minister announces three new Ebola treatment centres opening in Ituri.

Africa CDC declares outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS) under Article 3(F) of Africa CDC Statute. 395 suspected cases, 106 associated deaths reported. (Africa CDC PHECS declaration)

CDC and DHS invoke Title 42 travel restrictions; entry restrictions placed on non-US passport holders from DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan in previous 21 days. CDC moves 7 Americans (1 confirmed case + 6 high-risk contacts) to Germany for care. (CDC)
CDC current situation page confirms 9 health zones in Ituri Province now affected; EU announces PPE stockpiles ready for deployment and detection kit support to Africa CDC. (CDC; CNN)

Africa CDC formally declares outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS). CDC and DHS invoke Title 42 for at least 30 days restricting entry of non-US nationals who have been in DRC, Uganda or South Sudan within the previous 21 days. US moves 7 people (1 confirmed case, 6 high-risk contacts) from DRC to Germany for treatment/monitoring. US Embassy in Uganda temporarily suspends visa services. DRC Health Minister announces opening of 3 new Ebola treatment centres in affected region. WFP airlifts >5 tonnes of medical supplies to Ituri. OCHA reports 482 suspected cases and ~116 deaths in Ituri province alone.

OCHA reports 482+ suspected cases since April in Ituri; confirms Goma case; warns hostile environment (insecurity, displacement, hunger) is severely hampering response; >5 tonnes of supplies airlifted to Ituri by WFP.
UN News and NBC report outbreak approaching ~500 suspected cases and 116 associated deaths; case in Beni (North Kivu) also reported; situation remains rapidly evolving.

OCHA and UN partners warn hostile environment in eastern DRC is severely hampering response; nearly 10 million people in Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu face crisis-level hunger compounding outbreak risk. ECDC deploys expert to Africa CDC headquarters. Reuters witnesses Congolese nationals turned back at Bukavu-Rwanda border. Outbreak total now exceeds 482 suspected cases across at least 9 health zones per OCHA.

alerts.title: WHO PHEIC Declared — Bundibugyo Ebola, DRC & Uganda
alerts.body: WHO Director-General declared the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on 16–17 May 2026, citing cross-border spread, rapid increase in suspected cases and deaths, and a potentially much larger outbreak than currently detected. The declaration does not meet the criteria for a pandemic emergency.

alerts.title: Africa CDC PHECS Declared — 18 May 2026
alerts.body: Africa CDC declared the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security on 18 May 2026, empowering it to lead continental coordination. Africa CDC cited ~395 suspected cases and 106 deaths across DRC and Uganda, with high risk of further regional spread.

alerts.title: Ebola Confirmed in Goma (North Kivu) — Population >1 Million
alerts.body: INRB confirmed a Bundibugyo virus case in Goma, a rebel-held (M23) city of over one million on the DRC–Rwanda border, on 17–18 May 2026. The case is a woman who travelled from Bunia while already infected; Rwanda has closed Goma–Gisenyi border crossings indefinitely.

alerts.title: No Approved Vaccine or Therapeutic for Bundibugyo Virus
alerts.body: WHO, CDC, ECDC, and Africa CDC all confirm there are no approved vaccines or specific therapeutics for Bundibugyo virus; existing licensed Ebola vaccines (Ervebo, Zabdeno/Mvabea) target Zaire ebolavirus and are not considered effective against BDBV. Response relies entirely on supportive care and classic public-health containment.

alerts.title: US Title 42 Entry Restrictions Invoked — DRC, Uganda, South Sudan
alerts.body: CDC and DHS invoked Title 42 on 18 May 2026 for at least 30 days, restricting entry of non-US nationals who have been in DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan within the previous 21 days. An American missionary physician tested positive for Bundibugyo virus in Bunia on 17 May and is being transferred to Germany for treatment.

alerts.title: OCHA: 482 Suspected Cases & ~116 Deaths in Ituri Alone as of 19 May
alerts.body: OCHA reported on 19 May 2026 that more than 482 suspected cases and around 116 deaths have been recorded in Ituri Province since April — the highest figure yet published — and warned that insecurity and humanitarian crisis are severely hampering the response.

alerts.title: Healthcare-Worker Infections Signal IPC Gaps
alerts.body: At least 4 deaths among healthcare workers with symptoms consistent with haemorrhagic fever have been reported, and hospital-associated transmission is suspected. ECDC and WHO have flagged critical infection-prevention-and-control gaps in both formal and informal health facilities across Ituri.

alerts.title: Initial Xpert Tests Were False-Negative — Diagnosis Delay
alerts.body: Standard Ebola Xpert cartridges used at Bunia's provincial laboratory returned negative results for the first 20 samples because they were designed for Zaire ebolavirus; Bundibugyo virus was only confirmed after samples were forwarded to INRB Kinshasa, contributing to a 3–4 week detection lag.

news.title: OCHA: Eastern DRC Hostility Hampering Ebola Response; 482+ Suspected Cases
news.summary: OCHA warned on 19 May 2026 that insecurity, population displacement, and food crisis are severely complicating surveillance and response in Ituri. More than 482 suspected cases and ~116 deaths in Ituri alone have been reported since April, with WFP having airlifted 5+ tonnes of supplies to the province.

news.title: Africa CDC Declares Bundibugyo Ebola a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security
news.summary: Africa CDC officially declared a PHECS on 18 May 2026, citing ~395 suspected cases and 106 deaths across DRC and Uganda, and deep concern about regional spread toward Rwanda and South Sudan. The declaration empowers Africa CDC to lead and coordinate responses across AU member states.

news.title: American Missionary Physician Tests Positive in DRC; US Invokes Title 42
news.summary: Dr. Peter Stafford tested positive for Bundibugyo virus in Bunia on 17 May 2026; CDC confirmed an American was infected and is being transferred to Germany. CDC and DHS invoked Title 42 on 18 May restricting entry from DRC, Uganda and South Sudan for at least 30 days.

news.title: CDC Situation Update: 11 Confirmed, 336 Suspected, 88 Deaths in DRC as of 18 May
news.summary: CDC's current-situation page updated 18 May 2026 confirms 11 confirmed cases and 336 suspected cases including 88 deaths in DRC, and 2 confirmed cases including 1 death in Uganda, with the outbreak spanning 9 health zones in Ituri Province.

news.title: Ebola Confirmed in Rebel-Held Goma; Rwanda Closes Border Crossings
news.summary: INRB director Muyembe confirmed a Bundibugyo case in Goma, North Kivu — a city of over 1 million under M23 rebel control — on 17–18 May 2026. Rwanda immediately closed key Goma–Gisenyi border posts indefinitely, defying WHO guidance against blanket border closures.

news.title: NPR: Late US Notification and Funding Cuts Tied to Outbreak's Head Start
news.summary: NPR reports CDC only learned of the Ebola outbreak on 14 May, the day before it was announced, after the virus had been circulating for ~3 weeks undetected. Public health experts link the detection delay to cuts in USAID's DRC mission and shrinking WHO emergency capacity following US withdrawal.

news.title: WHO Declares Bundibugyo Ebola Outbreak a PHEIC Without Emergency Committee
news.summary: WHO Director-General Tedros declared a PHEIC on 16–17 May 2026 in an unprecedented move without first convening an Expert Emergency Committee, citing the gravity and pace of the outbreak. The outbreak does not yet meet pandemic emergency criteria under IHR.

news.title: STAT News: Number of Americans Exposed to Ebola in DRC Growing
news.summary: STAT News reported on 17 May that multiple US nationals in DRC are believed to have had exposure to suspected Ebola cases, with at least one developing symptoms. The US government arranged to transport exposed Americans to Germany, with some quarantined at a US military base.

news.title: WHO DON602: First Case a Healthcare Worker; False-Negative Tests Delayed Detection
news.summary: WHO's Disease Outbreak News (DON602) documents that standard Ebola Xpert tests at Bunia's provincial lab were negative for the first 20 samples because they target Zaire ebolavirus; BDBV was confirmed only after samples reached INRB Kinshasa, delaying the outbreak declaration by weeks.

news.title: LSHTM Rapid Reaction: Outbreak Exposes Gaps in Global Preparedness for Rare Filoviruses
news.summary: London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine experts warned on 18 May 2026 that the outbreak highlights the absence of broad-spectrum diagnostics, vaccines, and therapeutics covering non-Zaire Ebola species. They called for accelerated investment in multivalent filovirus countermeasures.

news.title: NBC News: No Vaccines or Treatments Exist for Bundibugyo; Experimental Candidates in Early Development
news.summary: NBC News reports that the only two licensed Ebola vaccines target Zaire ebolavirus and animal studies show they do not protect against Bundibugyo. A handful of experimental candidates — including an mRNA vaccine from China covering three Ebola strains — remain in early pre-clinical development with none in human trials.

news.title: Reuters: Health Workers Race to Reach DRC Frontlines; Uganda Postpones Martyrs' Day
news.summary: Reuters reports medical personnel mobilising to Ituri even as DRC's Congo Health Cluster records 105 suspected deaths and 393 suspected cases across nine Ituri health zones. Uganda postponed its Martyrs' Day celebration — which typically draws thousands of pilgrims from eastern DRC — due to outbreak risk.

background.virus: Bundibugyo virus (BDBV); formal species name Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense
background.discovery: 2007, during an outbreak in Bundibugyo District, Uganda; genomic sequencing confirmed a novel species distinct from Zaire ebolavirus by ~30% genetic divergence
background.case_fatality_rate_historical: 25–51% (WHO/CDC historical range for BDBV specifically; past BDBV outbreaks ranged 25–34%; WHO DON602 for current outbreak cites 30–50%); MSF and Johns Hopkins experts cite 25–40% for BDBV in current outbreak context
background.transmission: Direct contact with blood, body fluids, or tissues of infected people or animals; contact with contaminated surfaces, fomites, or bodies of deceased individuals. Individuals are infectious only when symptomatic. Fruit bats are the suspected zoonotic reservoir.
background.symptoms: Sudden fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache, sore throat — followed by vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, rash, impaired kidney/liver function, internal and external bleeding; nosebleeds and vomiting blood reported in current outbreak. CDC notes most current DRC cases are aged 20–39 and two-thirds are female.
background.vaccines_therapeutics: No WHO-approved or FDA-approved vaccines or specific therapeutics exist for Bundibugyo virus as of May 2026, confirmed by WHO, CDC, Africa CDC, and ECDC. The two licensed Ebola vaccines — Merck Ervebo and J&J Zabdeno/Mvabea — target Zaire ebolavirus; FDA has explicitly noted Ervebo is not considered effective for the spring 2026 Bundibugyo outbreak. Animal studies confirm poor cross-protection against BDBV. Candidate countermeasures in early development include: Mapp Biopharmaceutical MBP134 (non-human primate studies); an mRNA multivalent vaccine targeting BDBV and two other Ebola species published May 2026 in PNAS (pre-clinical mouse stage only, not in human trials); CEPI/Moderna/Oxford $26.7M multivalent mRNA and viral vector platform (pre-clinical). Africa CDC has activated a medical countermeasures workstream to assess available diagnostics, PPE, therapeutics, vaccines and cold-chain needs. All BDBV-specific candidates remain pre-licensure; supportive care (rehydration, oxygen, treating secondary infections) is the current standard of treatment.

past_outbreaks.notes: First identified outbreak; led to the discovery and naming of the Bundibugyo strain; genomic sequencing confirmed a novel Orthoebolavirus species.
Second documented Bundibugyo outbreak; contained within months in a remote area; second and last BDBV outbreak prior to 2026.

Second-largest Ebola outbreak in history, different species (Zaire ebolavirus), but same geographic zone and containment challenges (insecurity, mobile populations, mistrust); relevant precedent for current response difficulties.

past_outbreaks.location: Bulape Health Zone, Kasai Province, DRC (Ebola-Zaire)
past_outbreaks.notes: DRC's 16th Ebola outbreak, declared 4 September 2025 and over 1 December 2025; 53 confirmed, 11 probable cases; immediately preceded the current outbreak.

past_outbreaks.location: Ituri Province (epicentre), North Kivu Province (Goma, Beni), Kinshasa (retracted) — DRC; Kampala — Uganda
past_outbreaks.cfr: ~24% of suspected (true CFR undetermined pending full case ascertainment; BDBV historical range 25–50%)
past_outbreaks.notes: Third and largest Bundibugyo outbreak ever recorded; declared PHEIC by WHO 16–17 May 2026 and PHECS by Africa CDC 18 May 2026; at least 9 health zones in Ituri affected; spread confirmed to Goma and Beni in North Kivu and imported cases in Kampala, Uganda; no approved vaccine or therapeutic; detection delayed ~3 weeks due to false-negative standard Xpert tests.

why_this_matters: This is the largest Bundibugyo outbreak ever recorded, with 482+ suspected cases already more than triple the combined total of the two prior BDBV outbreaks (187 cases), and deaths exceeding those two outbreaks combined.

No approved vaccines or therapeutics exist for Bundibugyo virus; the two licensed Ebola vaccines target Zaire ebolavirus and are explicitly noted by the FDA and WHO as not effective for this outbreak, leaving response entirely dependent on classic public-health containment.

The outbreak has now spread beyond its Ituri epicentre to Goma and Beni in North Kivu — a city of over 1 million on the Rwandan border — sharply elevating the risk of cross-border transmission into Rwanda, Burundi, Tanzania, and beyond.

The outbreak zone is in the heart of an active armed conflict in eastern DRC; M23 rebels control Goma, severely impeding access, contact tracing, and the safe operation of treatment centres for one of the outbreak's newest hot spots.

Standard Ebola Xpert field tests returned false negatives for the first 20 samples because they were designed for Zaire ebolavirus, causing a 3–4 week diagnostic delay; Bundibugyo virus's ~30% genetic divergence from Zaire ebolavirus is a critical gap in current field-diagnostic infrastructure.

Healthcare-worker deaths (at least 4 confirmed) and suspected hospital-acquired transmission indicate critical IPC gaps, with the outbreak amplified through both formal and informal health facilities across Ituri.

A US citizen healthcare worker (Dr. Peter Stafford) has been confirmed infected in Bunia, prompting US Title 42 travel restrictions — only the second invocation of this authority in the modern era — and entry bans on non-US nationals from DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan.

Cuts to global public-health funding — including USAID DRC mission closure, reduced CDC capacity, and US withdrawal from WHO — have been directly linked by public-health experts and Oxfam to surveillance failures that allowed this outbreak to accumulate hundreds of cases before detection.

An Emergency Committee has yet to be convened (WHO Director-General acted unilaterally), and CEPI/Moderna/Oxford's multivalent BDBV mRNA vaccine platform — the most advanced candidate — remains in pre-clinical development with no human-trial timeline confirmed.
